2.4 Requesting and Taking Annual Leave
All annual leave must be requested through the human resources system and approved by the
employee's manager before any travel or other commitment is booked. Leave taken without prior
approval is treated as unauthorised absence under the attendance policy.
Requests must be submitted at least fourteen calendar days before the first day of leave. For a
continuous absence of more than five working days, the request must be submitted at least twenty-eight
calendar days in advance. Managers will respond to a request within five working days of receiving it.
Requests are considered in the order they are received. A manager may decline a request where the
absence would leave the team without adequate cover, where it falls in a published critical period such as
a financial close, or where the notice given is shorter than this policy requires. A declined request must be
explained in writing, and the manager should offer alternative dates.
A continuous absence of more than ten working days additionally requires approval from the relevant
director. Employees are asked to take at least ten days of their entitlement as a single continuous period
during the leave year.

Formal performance reviews take place twice a year. The mid-year review is held in July and is
developmental only. The year-end review is held in January, covers the full performance year, and
produces the employee's formal performance evaluation and rating.
The review process runs in four steps. The employee first completes a written self-assessment against
each objective. The manager then gathers written feedback from at least two colleagues who worked with
the employee during the period. The manager writes an evaluation and proposes a rating. Finally,
proposed ratings are moderated in a calibration meeting of managers at the same level, chaired by
People Operations, to ensure consistency across teams.
The manager discusses the moderated evaluation with the employee in a meeting, and the employee
may add written comments to the record. The completed evaluation is shared with the employee no later
than five working days after that meeting.
An employee who disagrees with their evaluation may request a review by their manager's manager
within ten working days of receiving it. The reviewing manager responds in writing within fifteen working
days, and that response concludes the process.

Performance is rated on a five-point scale: outstanding, exceeds expectations, meets expectations,
partially meets expectations, and does not meet expectations. Most employees performing well at their
level are rated as meeting expectations, and no quota is applied to any rating.

3.4 Outcome and Pay
A promotion takes effect from the first day of the month following the panel decision. Salary is adjusted to
at least the minimum of the new level's range, and the employee receives a written variation to their
contract of employment.
3 Promotion

3.2 Promotion Eligibility Requirements
To be eligible for promotion, an employee must meet all of the following requirements at the point of
nomination.
·  They have held their current role for at least twelve months of continuous service, and have
completed any probationary period
·  Their two most recent performance evaluations are rated at meets expectations or above, with at
least one rated exceeds expectations or above
·  They are not subject to an active performance improvement plan, and have no live formal disciplinary
warning on record
·  They have demonstrated the expectations of the next level in the career framework across at least
two consecutive quarters, evidenced by delivered work
·  Their manager supports the nomination, and a second manager at or above the target level endorses
it
Meeting the eligibility requirements does not guarantee promotion. Eligibility determines whether a
nomination can be considered; the decision itself rests with the promotion panel described in the next
section. Length of service alone is never grounds for promotion.
An employee who is not eligible may ask their manager for a written development plan setting out what
would need to change for eligibility to be met in a future cycle.
